about.title: Compton Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Compton sits at a busy crossroads of Los Angeles County, and its surface streets carry a lot of that traffic. In 2025, the city logged 333 injury collisions, with 484 people hurt and 3 lives lost. Public records show the heaviest collision counts along Compton Boulevard, Rosecrans Avenue, Alondra Boulevard, and Wilmington Avenue, and the numbers tend to climb on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., when commuters and weekend errands share the same lanes. If one of those crashes was yours, the days that follow can feel scattered: a car in the shop, appointments to schedule, calls from an adjuster you did not ask for. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent California attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened once, and we find someone equipped to review it.

whyChoose.title: Why Compton Drivers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city bus, county truck, or other government vehicle was involved, the window can shrink to six months. Getting connected early protects your options.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a crash, you may still recover damages reduced by your share. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to overstate your role.

items.title: Protect Your Evidence, Not Their File
items.desc: Photos, witness names, dashcam footage, and your own notes fade or disappear fast. The other driver's insurer may also ask for a recorded statement; you are not required to give one, and an attorney can handle that conversation for you.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company keeps calling me. Do I have to talk to them?
items.answer: No. You are not obligated to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and anything you say can be used to lower or deny your claim. It is reasonable to politely decline and let an attorney speak on your behalf. Your own insurer is a different matter, since your policy usually requires cooperation.

items.question: I was hit near the intersection of Compton Boulevard and Wilmington Avenue. Does where the crash happened matter?
items.answer: It can. Busy corridors like Compton Boulevard and Wilmington Avenue often have nearby businesses with cameras, traffic signal records, and multiple witnesses, all of which can help establish what occurred. An attorney can request that footage before it is overwritten, which frequently happens within days or weeks.

items.question: How much does it cost to be connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency. That means no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. California also places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary car accident claims, so those losses can be part of the conversation.
